import pandas as pd

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source6_31_0 and Source6_31_2 on 'batsman'
join_0_2 = pd.merge(source0, source2, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Operation 2: JOIN Source6_31_1 and Source6_31_6 on 'batsman'
join_1_6 = pd.merge(source1, source6, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Operation 3: JOIN Source6_31_3 and Source6_31_5 on 'batsman'
join_3_5 = pd.merge(source3, source5, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Operation 4: JOIN Source6_31_4 and Source6_31_5 on 'batsman'
join_4_5 = pd.merge(source4, source5, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Now perform the group by on Source6_31_0.batsman with the specified aggregations:
# avg(Source6_31_0.batsman_runs)
# sum(Source6_31_2.total_runs)
# avg(Source6_31_1.batsman_runs)
# sum(Source6_31_6.total_runs)
# avg(Source6_31_3.batsman_runs)
# sum(Source6_31_5.batsman_runs)
# sum(Source6_31_4.no of balls)
# sum(Source6_31_4.batsman_runs)
# avg(Source6_31_4.strike)

# We need to join all these aggregated results on batsman.
# The aggregation keys are all batsman from source0 (and others joined on batsman).

# Aggregate join_0_2:
agg_0_2 = join_0_2.groupby("batsman").agg(
    batsman_runs_x=("batsman_runs", "mean"),  # avg(Source6_31_0.batsman_runs)
    total_runs_x=("total_runs", "sum")        # sum(Source6_31_2.total_runs)
).reset_index()

# Aggregate join_1_6:
agg_1_6 = join_1_6.groupby("batsman").agg(
    batsman_runs_y=("batsman_runs", "mean"),  # avg(Source6_31_1.batsman_runs)
    total_runs_y=("total_runs", "sum")         # sum(Source6_31_6.total_runs)
).reset_index()

# Aggregate join_3_5:
agg_3_5 = join_3_5.groupby("batsman").agg(
    batsman_runs_x_5=("batsman_runs_x", "mean") if "batsman_runs_x" in join_3_5.columns else ("batsman_runs", "mean"),
    batsman_runs_y_7=("batsman_runs_y", "sum") if "batsman_runs_y" in join_3_5.columns else ("batsman_runs", "sum"),
).reset_index()

# But join_3_5 columns are ['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x', 'batsman_runs_y']? 
# Actually, source3 and source5 both have 'batsman' and 'batsman_runs'.
# After merge, columns are: batsman, batsman_runs_x (from source3), batsman_runs_y (from source5)
# So we can aggregate accordingly:
agg_3_5 = join_3_5.groupby("batsman").agg(
    batsman_runs_x_5=("batsman_runs_x", "mean"),  # avg(Source6_31_3.batsman_runs)
    batsman_runs_y_7=("batsman_runs_y", "sum")    # sum(Source6_31_5.batsman_runs)
).reset_index()

# Aggregate join_4_5:
# join_4_5 columns: batsman, no of balls, batsman_runs_x, strike, batsman_runs_y
# Actually source4 has ['batsman', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike']
# source5 has ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
# After merge, pandas will suffix to avoid collision:
# batsman_runs_x (from source4), batsman_runs_y (from source5)
agg_4_5 = join_4_5.groupby("batsman").agg(
    no_of_balls=("no of balls", "sum"),
    batsman_runs=("batsman_runs_x", "sum"),  # sum(Source6_31_4.batsman_runs)
    strike=("strike", "mean")                 # avg(Source6_31_4.strike)
).reset_index()

# Now join all aggregated dataframes on 'batsman' to form the final target table

# Start joining step by step:

# Join agg_0_2 and agg_1_6
df = pd.merge(agg_0_2, agg_1_6, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Join with agg_3_5
df = pd.merge(df, agg_3_5, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Join with agg_4_5
df = pd.merge(df, agg_4_5, on="batsman", how="outer")

# After merges, some batsman may have NaNs if they were missing in some sources.
# Fill NaNs with appropriate zeros or means:
# For runs and counts, fill NaN with 0
# For strike (float), fill NaN with 0.0

df["batsman_runs_x"] = df["batsman_runs_x"].fillna(0).astype(float)
df["total_runs_x"] = df["total_runs_x"].fillna(0).astype(int)
df["total_runs_y"] = df["total_runs_y"].fillna(0).astype(int)
df["batsman_runs_y"] = df["batsman_runs_y"].fillna(0).astype(float)  # originally mean, keep float
df["batsman_runs_x_5"] = df["batsman_runs_x_5"].fillna(0).astype(float)  # mean, keep float
df["batsman_runs_y_7"] = df["batsman_runs_y_7"].fillna(0).astype(int)
df["no_of_balls"] = df["no_of_balls"].fillna(0).astype(int)
df["batsman_runs"] = df["batsman_runs"].fillna(0).astype(int)
df["strike"] = df["strike"].fillna(0.0).astype(float)

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly:
# Target schema: ['batsman': string, 'batsman_runs_x': float, 'total_runs_x': integer, 'total_runs_y': integer,
# 'batsman_runs_y': integer, 'batsman_runs_x_5': integer, 'no of balls': integer, 'batsman_runs_y_7': integer,
# 'strike': float, 'batsman_runs': integer]

# Note: From aggregation, batsman_runs_y and batsman_runs_x_5 are floats (means),
# but target schema expects batsman_runs_y as integer and batsman_runs_x_5 as integer.
# We will round and convert to int accordingly.

df["batsman_runs_y"] = df["batsman_runs_y"].round().astype(int)
df["batsman_runs_x_5"] = df["batsman_runs_x_5"].round().astype(int)

# Rename 'no_of_balls' to 'no of balls' to match target schema
df = df.rename(columns={"no_of_balls": "no of balls"})

# Reorder columns to match target schema order exactly
df = df[
    [
        "batsman",
        "batsman_runs_x",
        "total_runs_x",
        "total_runs_y",
        "batsman_runs_y",
        "batsman_runs_x_5",
        "no of balls",
        "batsman_runs_y_7",
        "strike",
        "batsman_runs",
    ]
]

# Save the final dataframe to the target path
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
